codeflow.exclude.description: Glob patterns for files and folders CodeFlow does not analyze. node_modules is always skipped, and Rust analysis also skips target/. These patterns are combined with files.exclude.

codeflow.maxFiles.description: Maximum number of files CodeFlow analyzes for each language in each workspace folder. TypeScript and Rust are capped separately.

codeflow.view.defaultMode.description: Diagram opened by CodeFlow: Show Flow for Symbol at Cursor. focus draws the neighbourhood around the symbol (depth 2). workspace draws the whole graph and highlights the symbol. The toolbar toggle changes this for the open panel.

codeflow.view.maxNodes.description: Maximum number of nodes the diagram draws at once. Larger graphs show a notice and suggest focus mode.

codeflow.editor.followCursor.description: When the cursor moves in a TypeScript, JavaScript, or Rust file, highlight that symbol in the open diagram and pan to it. This does not lay the diagram out again.

codeflow.editor.refocusOnCursor.description: In focus mode, when the cursor moves to a symbol that is not in the current diagram, replace the diagram with that symbol's neighbourhood. When this is off, CodeFlow shows a not-in-view hint instead.

codeflow.editor.callDepth.description: How many call steps CodeFlow: Show Callers, CodeFlow: Show Callees, a request flow, and a sequence walk. The route itself is not a step.

codeflow.codeLens.enabled.description: Show caller and callee counts above each function and method. The counts are the call-graph degree. Uncertain calls are shown separately as “+N possible” and are not included in the main count. Clicking the caller count runs Show Callers. Clicking the callee count runs Show Callees.

codeflow.rust.useRustAnalyzer.description: When the rust-analyzer extension is installed and already running, use its call hierarchy to mark calls from the focused Rust symbol as certain. Tree-sitter still builds the graph when this is off or rust-analyzer is not active.
